sourceEvidence.label: ASB production-readiness source and validation collection

assessment.summary: Four structural opportunities cover service/process containment, credential renewal, long-term audit retention, and evidence-bound environment qualification; none is represented as implemented.

nonNegotiables: Preserve approval history, receipts, and operation identifiers across maintenance.
Do not claim real-environment qualification without a passing target evidence bundle.
assumptions: The current local approval profile remains single-host.
No measured latency, memory, recovery-time, or operator-budget target was supplied.
Untrusted computation is in scope for the operated runner profile.

opportunities.title: Contain services and descendant processes
opportunities.summary: Define explicit OS identities, socket ownership, and fail-closed descendant teardown.
opportunities.diagnosis: Service identity and descendant lifetime are owned by defaults rather than by one enforced runtime boundary.

evidence.claim: The agent and runner units do not declare service users or groups.
The runner socket is created with mode 0600.
Windows stop kills only the direct process.
A complete untrusted-runner profile needs pre-execution ownership of every descendant.

desiredInvariants: Services do not run as root in the ordinary profile.
Only the agent can access the runner endpoint.
Every Windows computation is contained before untrusted code executes.

options.title: Shared service identity with post-start Job assignment
options.summary: Run both Linux services as one static user and assign Windows children to a Job immediately after start.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: A static non-root user replaces the implicit identity.
The existing 0600 socket remains usable by the shared account.
A Job contains descendants after assignment, with a pre-assignment race.

tradeoffs.assessment: Removes routine root authority and contains most descendants; the services share an account and Windows has a launch race.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test local account isolation and an adversarial child-spawn race.

tradeoffs.assessment: No steady-state hop is added; Job setup affects launch only.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare p50 and p95 launch time on supported Windows hosts.

tradeoffs.assessment: One Job handle is retained per active process.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure handle count and working set under maximum concurrency.

tradeoffs.assessment: Descendants terminate together after Job assignment.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run cancellation and crash tests with child and grandchild processes.

tradeoffs.assessment: Packages must create an account and own runtime/log directories.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise install, upgrade, restart, and rollback.

tradeoffs.assessment: One account preserves current socket semantics.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test ownership migration from current installations.

residualRisks: Agent and runner share account-level authority.
A child may execute before Job assignment.

acceptanceCriteria: Services run without root and authorized socket calls succeed.
All descendants created after assignment exit on cancellation.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Restore old unit files and process helper, then restore file ownership.

options.title: Split service identities with fail-closed Job launch
options.summary: Use distinct Linux users with a systemd-owned socket and create Windows children suspended until assigned to a Job.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Separate static identities bound service authority.
Socket activation provides explicit group ownership and inherited listener semantics.
Suspended launch prevents untrusted code from running before Job assignment.

tradeoffs.assessment: Separates service authority and closes the Windows pre-assignment window.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Verify socket denial and process-tree teardown on real targets.

tradeoffs.assessment: Socket activation and suspended launch add setup work.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure p95 launch latency and socket request latency.

tradeoffs.assessment: Adds bounded socket-manager state and one Job handle per run.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure handles and working set at concurrency limit.

tradeoffs.assessment: Containment setup fails closed, though new packaging and launcher paths can fail.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Fault-inject socket activation and every Windows launch stage.

tradeoffs.assessment: Two users, group policy, socket unit, and Windows diagnostics add operational work.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run clean install, upgrade, and incident exercises.

tradeoffs.assessment: Ownership and listener semantics require a staged migration.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Prove upgrade and rollback with preserved configs and logs.

residualRisks: Selected runner capabilities may still be excessive.
Nested Windows Job and legacy OS behavior require target qualification.

acceptanceCriteria: Agent alone can call the runner socket.
No untrusted instruction runs before Job assignment.
Cancellation removes the full process tree.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable socket activation, restore prior units and ownership, and revert the launcher.

opportunities.recommendation: Use the split-identity, suspended-launch design for untrusted computation; retain the shared-user design only as a named interim profile.

opportunities.title: Renew local trust without losing history
opportunities.summary: Separate credential and bootstrap-token lifetime from durable approval state.
opportunities.diagnosis: One initialization boundary currently couples expiring secrets to long-lived state.

evidence.claim: The local trust set expires after one year, the CA key is not persisted, and the UI token is a persistent file.
Safe renewal requires generation replacement that leaves the SQLite state and receipts in place.

desiredInvariants: Rotation does not modify durable application history.
Only a complete validated credential generation becomes active.
Bootstrap-token exposure can be remediated independently.

options.title: Offline atomic generation rotation
options.summary: Rotate complete credential generations and the bootstrap token during a maintenance window without moving state.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Atomic generation replacement renews certificates and independently invalidates the bootstrap token.

tradeoffs.assessment: Removes expiry-driven state abandonment and limits token exposure after rotation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Fault-inject every write and verify old-or-new complete loading.

tradeoffs.assessment: No steady-state request-path work is added.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure maintenance duration for representative directories.

tradeoffs.assessment: One bounded rollback generation is retained on disk.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure disk use and enforce the configured generation count.

tradeoffs.assessment: Atomic activation supports rollback but requires planned downtime.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test interrupted rotation and failed restart recovery.

tradeoffs.assessment: Operators gain stop, rotate, restart, verify, and cleanup steps.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run the documented procedure on every supported OS.

tradeoffs.assessment: A versioned layout can preserve v1 state while changing credential files.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test v1 read, first rotation, rollback, and backup restore.

residualRisks: A compromised host may already have copied active secrets.
Cross-platform locking and ACL behavior require qualification.

workPackages: Implement maintenance commands and atomic swap.
acceptanceCriteria: State and receipt bytes remain unchanged across rotation.
Old token is rejected after the documented restart boundary.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Switch to the previous validated generation without rolling back state.

options.title: Online overlapping trust generations
options.summary: Coordinate current and next trust generations across independently restarted participants.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Overlapping generations support renewal and token retirement without coordinated downtime.

tradeoffs.assessment: Enables rotation but temporarily trusts more keys and adds controller authority.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test compromise and retirement behavior for old generations.

tradeoffs.assessment: Dual verification adds work during overlap.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark handshake and session validation during overlap.

tradeoffs.assessment: Two live trust bundles and acknowledgement state are retained.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure memory and disk with maximum overlap.

tradeoffs.assessment: Avoids planned outage but introduces partial-rollout states.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Fault-inject each acknowledgement and timeout path.

tradeoffs.assessment: Scheduling, monitoring, retirement, and incident response become necessary.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run a full rotation and rollback exercise.

tradeoffs.assessment: Wire/session generation semantics and controller state must migrate together.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise mixed-version participants.

residualRisks: Old credentials remain valid during overlap.
Controller compromise can influence trust retirement.

acceptanceCriteria: All required participants move generations without lost state.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Reactivate the old generation before the overlap deadline.

opportunities.recommendation: Use offline atomic rotation for the current single-host profile; adopt overlap only for a documented zero-downtime or multi-host requirement.

opportunities.title: Retain audit history beyond online limits
opportunities.summary: Separate full long-term evidence from the bounded online recovery working set.
opportunities.diagnosis: Full online rows currently serve both retry recovery and long-term audit retention, making safe uptime finite.

evidence.claim: The store rejects new work at fixed operation, mutation, and replay caps and does not compact terminal history.
Deleting full rows safely requires a retained identifier and result policy that prevents duplicate execution.

desiredInvariants: Pending and uncertain work is never compacted.
Only verified durable archives authorize deletion of full online rows.

options.title: Verified export without reclamation
options.summary: Create restore-checked archive bundles and capacity status while leaving online rows untouched.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Verified exports preserve evidence but do not reclaim bounded online capacity.

tradeoffs.assessment: Adds integrity and restore evidence without changing retry semantics.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Restore every produced bundle and compare semantic counts and digests.

tradeoffs.assessment: Export and restore add periodic I/O outside the request path.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure export duration and request latency under load.

tradeoffs.assessment: A temporary restored database and buffers are required.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak RSS during maximum-size export verification.

tradeoffs.assessment: Online failure behavior remains unchanged and finite capacity remains.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Fill to the cap after repeated exports.

tradeoffs.assessment: Operators must monitor capacity and protect archives.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise backup alerts and restore drills.

tradeoffs.assessment: The change is additive and does not alter stored rows.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Verify old binaries still open the database.

residualRisks: Admission still stops at the existing caps.
Archive durability depends on operator custody.

workPackages: Add canonical export, manifest, hashes, and verifier.
acceptanceCriteria: A restored export matches source semantic counts and digests.
Export failure never changes online rows.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable export scheduling; no data rollback is required.

options.title: Verified compaction with identifier tombstones
options.summary: Archive eligible terminal rows and replace them transactionally with exact identifiers and minimal retained outcomes.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Verified compaction reclaims payload capacity while tombstones preserve non-reuse and retry semantics.

tradeoffs.assessment: Preserves identifier non-reuse if tombstones are exact; archive custody becomes security-critical.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Replay archived IDs and corrupt archives under fault injection.

tradeoffs.assessment: A smaller DB may help requests while compaction adds I/O and archive lookup.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark p95 request latency before, during, and after compaction.

tradeoffs.assessment: Adds an archive catalog, tombstone index, and verification workspace.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure index growth and peak RSS.

tradeoffs.assessment: Removes fixed payload lifetime but adds archive and compaction failure modes.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Crash at every protocol stage and prove old-or-new completeness.

tradeoffs.assessment: Retention, compaction, restore, and archive incidents need runbooks.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run quarterly restore and lost-archive exercises.

tradeoffs.assessment: Schema, retry semantics, and rehydration change.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Migrate a cap-sized copy and roll it back from archive.

residualRisks: Archive loss prevents full historical retrieval.

acceptanceCriteria: Pending and uncertain records never compact.
Crash leaves a complete online or archived record.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable new compaction and rehydrate previously compacted batches from verified archives.

opportunities.recommendation: Build verified export first, then enable tombstone compaction only after restore and retry semantics are proven on the selected archive destination.

opportunities.title: Make qualification an evidence-producing gate
opportunities.summary: Bind every deployment claim to immutable inputs, a real target, mandatory exercises, and a verifiable bundle.
opportunities.diagnosis: Current checks are carefully scoped but lack one machine-readable profile result that fails on unavailable mandatory evidence.

evidence.claim: The validation record labels the result Developer Preview and lists unqualified properties.
Real-environment claims require a profile-specific target and evidence boundary.

desiredInvariants: Every claim is bound to immutable inputs and target facts.
Unavailable mandatory checks fail the profile result.
Evidence bundles exclude secrets and can be independently verified.

options.title: Repository qualification bundle
options.summary: Run profile-specific mandatory checks on real targets and emit hashed, redacted, machine-readable evidence.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: A profile fails when real mandatory checks are missing and binds results to target facts.

tradeoffs.assessment: Prevents local or cross-build evidence from being promoted beyond its target.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Verify failure on missing mandatory checks and tampered artifacts.

tradeoffs.assessment: Qualification adds target runtime outside production requests.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure each profile duration against CI budgets.

tradeoffs.assessment: Logs and bundles consume bounded artifact storage.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure bundle size and enforce redacted retention limits.

tradeoffs.assessment: Repeatable manifests make drift and missing evidence visible.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Replay verification on a separate host.

tradeoffs.assessment: Profiles, runners, redaction, retention, and signing need ownership.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run release and incident exercises.

tradeoffs.assessment: Existing tests can be wrapped incrementally.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare wrapped results with current workflows.

residualRisks: Test omissions can still produce a narrow but incomplete profile.
The operator remains trusted to control the target.

implementationReadiness.rollback: Withdraw the profile claim and continue existing tests while fixing the harness.

options.title: Independent lab qualification track
options.summary: Run the same immutable candidate and profile under independent custody and review.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Independent custody strengthens claims that explicitly require external validation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Separates project implementation from qualification custody.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Audit chain of custody and reproduce a sample result.

tradeoffs.assessment: Transfer, scheduling, and review add release latency.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure lead time over several qualification cycles.

tradeoffs.assessment: The lab retains duplicate evidence and review records.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure storage per cycle.

tradeoffs.assessment: External scheduling can block time-sensitive releases.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Define and test expiry and exception handling.

tradeoffs.assessment: Contracts, policy governance, reviewers, and renewal are required.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run a complete mock certification cycle.

tradeoffs.assessment: A stable immutable candidate and acceptance policy are prerequisites.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Freeze and qualify a disposable release candidate.

residualRisks: Independent review is only as complete as the published profile.
Cost and availability may limit frequency.

acceptanceCriteria: A reviewer can reproduce the bundle and scope the claim.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Expire or withdraw the external claim without changing the artifact.

opportunities.recommendation: Adopt repository qualification bundles now and reserve independent lab qualification for claims that explicitly require it.

openQuestions: Select package account names and supported Linux distributions.
Select archive destination, encryption, retention, and custody policy.
Select supported Windows versions and real qualification targets.
Name the authority that signs and reviews qualification bundles.
